validated_results.title: Metabolism and growth inhibitory activity of cranberry derived flavonoids in bladder cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: This study evaluated cranberry-derived flavonoids exclusively in human bladder tumour and uroepithelial cell lines, providing no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Metabolism and growth inhibitory activity of cranberry derived flavonoids in bladder cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: Quercetin and its metabolites were tested only in in vitro bladder cancer cell lines, so no human cancer incidence was assessed.

validated_results.title: Extra-virgin olive oil phenols block cell cycle progression and modulate chemotherapeutic toxicity in bladder cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: Extra-virgin olive oil phenol effects were assessed solely in T24 and 5637 bladder cancer cell lines, with no human incidence analysis.

validated_results.title: Extra-virgin olive oil phenols block cell cycle progression and modulate chemotherapeutic toxicity in bladder cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: The report is an in vitro cell-line experiment on olive oil polyphenol extract and provides no original human epidemiological estimate.

validated_results.title: Promoter CpG island methylation in ion transport mechanisms and associated dietary intakes jointly influence the risk of clear-cell renal cell cancer.
validated_results.reason: The report centers on a genotype-stratified or gene-exposure interaction, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: Vitamin D3 Intake Dose and Common Cancer: A Population-Based Case Control Study in a Chinese Population.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting an adjusted odds ratio for bladder cancer associated with vitamin D3 use.

extraction.timing: cases identified January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2011; insurance data January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2011
extraction.population: Chinese population identified from Catastrophic Illness Patient Database and longitudinal health insurance database

sample_size.excerpt: Results: There were 1.21% (1961/161806) patients in cases and 0.67 % (1092/161806) patients in controls identified were vitamin D3 users.
sample_size.location: Results; total_n derived from reported group counts 161806 + 161806 = 323612

effect_size.excerpt: Among these, the risk of kidney cancer and bladder cancer associated with intakes of vitamin D3 were significant (OR 2.59; 95% CI 1.81-3.70; OR 4.97; 95% CI 4.40-5.60) in an adjusted model.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among these, the risk of kidney cancer and bladder cancer associated with intakes of vitamin D3 were significant (OR 2.59; 95% CI 1.81-3.70; OR 4.97; 95% CI 4.40-5.60) in an adjusted model.

comparison.excerpt: Use of vitamin D3 was compared between two groups.

design.excerpt: A population-based retrospective case-control study was conducted

timing.excerpt: from January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2011and January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2011, respectively

continent.excerpt: This study aimed to investigate whether vitamin D is associated with risk of common cancers in Chinese population.

ethnicity.excerpt: A Population-Based Case Control Study in a Chinese Population

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Odds ratios (ORs) were employed to quantify the risk associated with exposure to vitamin D3 by logistic regression.

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_supporting_text: A Population-Based Case Control Study in a Chinese Population
